description: Runner with hamstring history training for first 50-miler asks if they should do a 26-mile training run this weekend. Active hamstring tightness flagged earlier in the week. Dean must give a specific recommendation — not dodge.

user.name: Tobias
user.injury_notes: History: left hamstring grade 2 strain, July 2024 — required 8 weeks off. Currently reporting tightness in the same left hamstring, rated 2/10, noticed on Tuesday's tempo. Active monitoring.
user.injury_history: Left hamstring grade 2 strain July 2024 — 8 weeks off running. Fully recovered. Now reporting mild tightness same side.

recent_conversation.content: Felt a little tightness in my left hamstring during the tempo yesterday. Like a 2/10. Probably just tired.

Left hamstring tightness at 2/10 on tempo day — same side as your grade 2 strain from last year. That's worth tracking carefully. The 'probably just tired' read might be right, but given the history, let's treat this as a real signal until it proves otherwise. How does it feel this morning?

inbound_sms: Hamstring is still a 2/10 today, maybe a tiny bit better. I have a 26 mile training run planned for Saturday. Should I do it?

ground_truth.notes: Tobias is asking a direct decision question: should he do his 26-mile training run with 2/10 hamstring tightness and a grade 2 strain history on the same side. Dean MUST give a direct recommendation — not 'it depends' or 'listen to your body'. Core passing criteria (score 7+): (1) clear recommendation NOT to do the full 26-miler, with a reason tied to the hamstring history — any specific alternative is acceptable: shortening to 10-16 miles, pushing to next week, swapping for easy miles — ALL of these are correct answers and must NOT be penalized; (2) name WHY the history matters — grade 2 scar tissue + current tightness = elevated re-strain risk at high mileage; (3) prescribe AT LEAST 2 specific named hamstring exercises from the list provided — 'Nordic curls', 'single-leg RDLs', etc. with sets/reps. The exercises and the specific recommendation are both required to pass. A response of 'yes go for it' scores 0. A response that says 'be careful' without a specific recommendation scores below 4. A response with a recommendation but no named exercises scores below 6. IMPORTANT: Shortening the run (e.g., to 10-16 miles) IS a correct and safe recommendation — do NOT penalize it. Dean is not required to set plan_action.lighter_week for this fixture, but doing so is also acceptable — do not penalize its presence.
